title: Home Server
desc: The machine behind everything else here: an i7-7700 with 16 GB of RAM and an RTX 2060 Super, two 512 GB SSDs mirrored in RAID 1 for data, and a separate 512 GB boot SSD. Set up with Tailscale for access from anywhere and a dedicated access point router, then wired up as the box that runs the apps, the storage, and the agents.
row_text: Home server: RAID storage and a local model endpoint

title: Agastya
desc: The Agastya embeddings system: a decision model walks a document's table of contents section by section, and embeddings rank the leaves it keeps. No training and no labels, point it at a book and it navigates. Benchmarked against published STAIR baselines on the public SearchTome set.
row_text: Agastya: navigating a book by embeddings

title: Automated Bin
desc: An automatic bin built with an Arduino, an IR sensor, and a servo motor: a compact exercise in sensing the physical world and acting on it.

title: Automated Garden
desc: A self-tending garden on an Arduino Mega, with soil-moisture, rain, and light sensors deciding when to water. It later evolved into the mini greenhouse, now listed under Projects.

title: Radar Project
desc: A radar built from an Arduino Mega, an IR sensor, an LCD display, and a servo motor: sweep, range, and a live readout fed by continuous data.
row_text: Radar: sweep and range on an LCD

title: 12V → 5V DC Converter
desc: A step-down converter built to run 5-volt microcontrollers inside 12-volt projects. The first project I ever posted, and a clean lesson in the fundamentals.

title: Marks Sender
desc: A utility that reads marks from a spreadsheet and automatically emails them out to students. My first project with a public code repository.
row_text: Marks Sender: spreadsheet to email, automated

title: Smart Security System
desc: A home-security system built around a Raspberry Pi 3b+, with camera and sensing on a full Linux stack, and a practical grounding in embedded systems.
row_text: Smart Security: a Raspberry Pi security system
